advances:
This does not prove contact balance or (SRD).  It proves the exact
reflected-cap consequence of full midpoint containment, with the actual
optimizer and every actual contact choice retained, and reduces contact
balance to the strictly stronger simultaneous three-direction condition
(SRD).  The proof identifies (SRD) as the precise unsupported step.
author: mp_r236_cb_direct
proof:
Fix \(\ell\).  The two cap sets on the left of (2) are compact and
convex, possibly of area zero.  Full compatibility gives
\[
\frac{A_j+A_k}{2}\subseteq A_1.
\]
For a point from each displayed cap, its \(q_\ell\)-coordinate after
averaging is at most
\[
\frac{c_\ell+d_\ell}{2}=\rho_\ell.
\]
This proves (2).  The middle cap on the right has area \(p_\ell\), by
accepted fact `58b8e7bb5c3be36f`.  Planar Brunn--Minkowski applied to
(2) gives (3), including degenerate endpoint caps.

For (4), first suppose \(b_\ell>0\).  The contact identity and the actual
optimizer classification give
\[
c_\ell+Q_{k,q_\ell}(v_\ell)
=E_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\le2\rho_\ell.
\tag{8}
\]
The inequality is equality in the crossing and middle-capacity regimes;
it may be strict only in the outer-capacity regime \(b_\ell=m\).
Thus \(Q_{k,q_\ell}(v_\ell)\le d_\ell\), and cap monotonicity gives
\[
w_\ell=F_{k,q_\ell}(d_\ell)\ge v_\ell.
\]
If \(b_\ell=0\), then \(u_\ell=v_\ell=0\).  The zero-demand endpoint
case in accepted fact `65512ded3a06d971` gives
\[
2\rho_\ell\le
Q_{j,q_\ell}(0)+Q_{k,q_\ell}(0),
\]
so \(d_\ell\le Q_{k,q_\ell}(0)\) and \(w_\ell=0=v_\ell\).  This proves
(4) without replacing the actual value \(E_q(0)=-\infty\) by its finite
extension.

Now assume \(W>0\) and (5).  From (1),
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell d_\ell
=2W-\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell c_\ell>0.
\tag{9}
\]
If a point \(x\) lay outside all halfplanes (6), then
\[
0=\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell q_\ell\right)\cdot x
>\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell d_\ell>0,
\]
a contradiction.  Hence (6) covers the plane.  Intersecting with
\(A_k\), taking areas, and using subadditivity gives (7).

The contact sets are compact and the maps in (1) are continuous, so the
minimum in (SRD) is attained.  If contact balance failed under \(W>0\),
then every contact choice would satisfy (5).  If (SRD) were available,
apply it to its minimizing choice.  Equation (7) would give the opposite
weak inequality, a contradiction.  Thus (SRD) would prove
\[
\max_{u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)}
\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)\ge0.
\]

No derivation of (SRD) from full midpoint containment is presently
available.  Directionwise Brunn--Minkowski gives only the three separate
bounds
\[
w_\ell\le
\left(2\sqrt{p_\ell}-\sqrt{u_\ell}\right)^2,
\tag{10}
\]
which follow from (3).  It does not select the three contacts jointly and
does not force the strict sum in (SRD).

This logical gap is visible even inside exact residual area arithmetic.
Normalize
\[
M=1,\qquad m=\frac14,\qquad a_1=1,\qquad t=\frac12.
\]
Then \(r=1/4\), \(s=1\) lies strictly in the residual strip.  The exact
scalar data
\[
p_\ell=\frac13,\qquad
b_\ell=\frac16,\qquad
u_\ell=v_\ell=\frac1{12},\qquad
w_\ell=\frac14
\qquad(\ell=1,2,3)
\tag{11}
\]
satisfy \(p_\ell+b_\ell=t\), \(0\le u_\ell\le b_\ell\le m\),
\(w_\ell\ge v_\ell\), and even the reflected inequalities (3), since
\[
\frac{2}{\sqrt3}
\ge \frac1{2\sqrt3}+\frac12.
\]
Nevertheless
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3w_\ell=\frac34>\frac14=m.
\]
The data (11) are not asserted to be geometrically realizable; they prove
that the residual scalar constraints plus all separate same-direction
Brunn--Minkowski rows cannot imply (SRD).  A proof of (SRD) must use the
simultaneous geometry of the three reflected caps, or an equivalent
cross-direction consequence of
\((A_j+A_k)/2\subseteq A_1\).
statement:
Use all notation and conventions of accepted fact `58b8e7bb5c3be36f`.
For arbitrary choices
\[
u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)
\qquad(\ell=1,2,3),
\]
put
\[
c_\ell=Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell),\qquad
d_\ell=2\rho_\ell-c_\ell,\qquad
w_\ell=F_{k,q_\ell}(d_\ell).
\tag{1}
\]
Then, including zero demand, capacity demand, and nonunique contacts,
\[
\frac{
 \bigl(A_j\cap\{q_\ell\cdot x\le c_\ell\}\bigr)+{}
 \bigl(A_k\cap\{q_\ell\cdot x\le d_\ell\}\bigr)}
 {2}
\subseteq
A_1\cap\{q_\ell\cdot x\le\rho_\ell\},
\tag{2}
\]
and hence
\[
2\sqrt{p_\ell}\ge \sqrt{u_\ell}+\sqrt{w_\ell}.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(v_\ell=b_\ell-u_\ell\), then
\[
w_\ell\ge v_\ell.
\tag{4}
\]

Moreover, if \(W>0\) and
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^3\alpha_\ell c_\ell<0,
\tag{5}
\]
then the three reflected lower halfplanes
\[
\{x:q_\ell\cdot x\le d_\ell\}
\tag{6}
\]
cover \(\mathbb R^2\), and therefore
\[
m\le\sum_{\ell=1}^3 w_\ell.
\tag{7}
\]

Consequently, contact balance would follow from the following exact
simultaneous reflected-cap deficit:
\[
\boxed{
W>0\ \Longrightarrow\
\min_{\substack{u_\ell\in\mathcal U_{q_\ell}(b_\ell)\\ \ell=1,2,3}}
\sum_{\ell=1}^3
F_{k,q_\ell}\!\left(
 2\rho_\ell-Q_{j,q_\ell}(u_\ell)
\right)<m.}
\tag{SRD}
\]
Condition (SRD) is not claimed here.
